Personality: Ovius Calavius, a prominent figure of the Calavii, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Ovius Calavius owes allegiance to the Roman Republic (SPQR), hailing from the noble house of Calavii. Historical Record: A kinsman of Pacuvius Calavius, head of the Calavii, an Italic house of the Roman Republic. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
